why: I checked all eight expect lines and their proofs. Each one can be checked in the repo at the PR head. Five are CLI runs of `printf ... | node bin/csv2json.js [--tsv]` with an exact expected output and exit code. One is a `node -e` run that imports src/parse.js and deep-equals the result. One is `npm test` plus a grep and a read of the test file for a `--tsv` CLI test. The last is a read of README.md for a `--tsv` usage example. Every line names a specific output or artifact, so one careful reader gets one answer. Every proof is a run or read at head. No line depends on a release, a deploy or a published page. "Publishing a release" appears only as a non-goal. Some proofs are loose: the comma-field run doesn't check the trailing newline with od. Each one still checks its line at head.
